question: transition vs animation — when each?
shortAnswer: transitions interpolate property changes; animations use keyframes for sequenced/looping motion.
detailedAnswer: Transitions for UI state; keyframes for loader/entrance choreography.

question: Which properties are 'cheap' to animate?
shortAnswer: Prefer transform and opacity (compositor-friendly); avoid layout-thrashing top/left/width.
detailedAnswer: will-change sparingly. Measure jank on low-end devices.

question: Explain animation-fill-mode.
shortAnswer: Controls values before/after execution (none, forwards, backwards, both).
detailedAnswer: forwards keeps final keyframe styles. Without it, elements may snap back.

question: How do you respect prefers-reduced-motion?
shortAnswer: Wrap motion in @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) or reduce to instant opacity.
detailedAnswer: Essential info must not rely on motion alone. Provide pause for long animations.

question: easing functions — why not always linear?
shortAnswer: Perceived realism and UI polish; ease-out for exits, ease-in-out for moves.
detailedAnswer: Custom cubic-bezier for brand motion. Overshoot carefully for restraint.

question: How do you debug a transition that doesn't run?
shortAnswer: Check if property is animatable, values comparable, specificity, display:none toggles, reduced motion.
detailedAnswer: display can't interpolate; use opacity/visibility patterns or @starting-style.

question: What is @keyframes composition with multiple animations?
shortAnswer: Multiple animations on one element via comma-separated lists; watch conflicting properties.
detailedAnswer: animation shorthand order matters. Name collisions across bundles.

question: Scroll-driven animations — concept?
shortAnswer: Tie animation progress to scroll timelines instead of time.
detailedAnswer: Powerful for storytelling; still honor reduced motion and performance budgets.

question: GPU layers and will-change pitfalls?
shortAnswer: will-change can promote layers but wastes memory if overused.
detailedAnswer: Add only around interaction, remove after. Don't will-change: everything.

question: Design motion guidelines for a product.
shortAnswer: Durations scale, easing tokens, reduced-motion policy, when motion is allowed.
detailedAnswer: Codify in DS. Avoid novelty animations that delay task completion.

question: How do enter/exit animations work with display:none?
shortAnswer: Historically hard; modern approaches include @starting-style, WAAPI, or keep in DOM briefly.
detailedAnswer: Libraries often manage mount/unmount timing. Accessibility: don't delay focus too long.

question: FLIP technique at a high level?
shortAnswer: First/Last/Invert/Play — animate transforms to simulate layout changes cheaply.
detailedAnswer: Useful for shared-element-like rearrangements without animating layout props.
